reasons: A clear message is shown when the run record fails to load.
No test is visible in this file or the packet.
The replay start time can be set from the page address in development builds, which is a debugging aid and not part of normal use.

terms.meaning: A library for building web pages out of reusable parts that redraw when their data changes.
A drawing area in the browser where code paints shapes pixel by pixel.
A React function that lets a component remember values or fetch data.
Values a component remembers, which cause a redraw when they change.
A stored value that survives redraws without causing one.
Asking the server for fresh data again at a set interval.
A browser call that runs a piece of code just before each screen refresh, used for smooth animation.
In this file, the current position in the run's list of stages and how far along it the run is.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the pieces it needs
sections.what: Brings in React helpers, the page router, icons, the reduced-motion check, the data hook, the shared types and the drawing engine. It shows nothing to the user by itself.
sections.why: Likely reason: the rest of the file uses these pieces, so they are loaded first.

sections.name: TOOL_LABEL, DONE, fmt
sections.title: Labels, finished statuses and number format
sections.what: Holds the display names for the two tools, the list of statuses that count as a finished stage, and a helper that writes numbers with thousands separators. It also states the rule that every tile is one recorded datapoint.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps these small fixed values in one place so the wording stays the same everywhere.
sections.watch_out: The finished list matches status words such as succeeded and skipped, so a new status from the server would not count as finished.

sections.name: stageDurations
sections.title: How long each stage plays in replay
sections.what: Gives each stage a playback length between about 2.6 and 5.5 seconds, based on how long that stage really took. Long stages play longer, but the scale is compressed so they do not dominate.
sections.why: Likely reason: a real run can take many minutes, so the replay is squeezed into a short viewing time.
sections.watch_out: If start or finish times are missing, the shortest length is used, so a bad record makes the replay look rushed.

sections.name: phaseProgress
sections.title: How far each phase has progressed
sections.what: Turns the current stage and how far through it the run is into a percentage for each of the five phases: scope, gather, check, compute and compose. A phase with no stages counts as finished once a later phase has started.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the completion rule. The drawing engine needs one number per phase, so this converts the stage list into those numbers.
sections.watch_out: Changing the rule for phases with no stages changes when the drawing moves on to the next phase.

sections.name: liveCursor
sections.title: Estimating progress in a live stage
sections.what: While a run is live, finds the first stage that has not finished and estimates how far through it the run is, using the time since that stage started. The estimate rises toward the end without reaching it, and a failed stage is shown halfway.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server gives only start times, so progress between refreshes has to be estimated.
sections.watch_out: The time scale of 25 seconds is a fixed guess, so the progress can look faster or slower than the real stage.

sections.name: caption
sections.title: Caption text for each phase
sections.what: Writes the heading and sentence under the field for the current phase. The sentences fill in counts of projects, countries, datapoints, sourced and verified items, flagged items, selected items and slides. Lessons Learnt runs get different wording.
sections.why: Likely reason: the caption explains the picture in plain words as the animation moves on.
sections.watch_out: Slides citing 1 to 30 projects count as focused and the rest count as overview slides, so changing that range changes the wording.

sections.name: LEGEND
sections.title: Colour key
sections.what: Lists the colours and names shown in the legend: cost, schedule, capacity and scope, other, flagged, feeds the output, and no source.
sections.why: Likely reason: readers need a key to understand the colours in the picture.
sections.watch_out: The same colours are also set in the drawing engine, so a change in one place can leave the two out of step.

sections.name: CollationField (part 1)
sections.title: Setup of state, data and mode
sections.what: Sets up what the component remembers, loads the run record, and chooses live, replay or finished mode. It also creates the drawing engine and tells it when the canvas changes size or scrolls out of view.
sections.why: Likely reason: pausing the drawing when it is off screen saves work, and the size watcher keeps the canvas sharp.
sections.watch_out: The replay start time is read from the page address only in development builds, so production always starts at the beginning.

sections.name: CollationField: if
sections.title: Animation driver
sections.what: Runs the animation one frame at a time. In live mode it reads progress from the run. In replay mode it moves a timeline that can play, pause or jump. When the animation reaches the end it calls the finish callback once, after a short pause.
sections.why: Likely reason: the picture must follow either the live run or the timeline on every frame.
sections.watch_out: The finish callback is guarded so it fires once; a restart resets that guard, so the callback can fire again on a later replay.

sections.name: CollationField (part 3)
sections.title: Page layout
sections.what: Draws the canvas and its overlays: the top bar with the mode label and the play, skip or replay buttons, the loading and error text, the stage list, the caption, the legend and the hover panel.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the exact arrangement. It is the visible frame around the picture.
sections.watch_out: The replay button appears only once the run has finished, so a live run shows no replay control.

sections.name: FieldTooltip
sections.title: Hover panel
sections.what: Shows a small panel when the pointer is over a slide or a project. A slide panel shows its title and the first few projects it cites. A project panel shows counts of sourced, verified, flagged and used datapoints, and says that clicking opens the project.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets someone check a point in the picture without leaving the view.
sections.watch_out: Every mouse movement recounts the datapoints of the project under the pointer, so very large projects could make hovering feel slow.

summary: A React component that draws an animated picture of one Reality Scan or Lessons Learnt run, either live while it runs, as a replay of its record, or as the finished picture.
purpose: Shows how a run gathered, checked and selected its datapoints and then produced slides. It also shows the stage list, a caption for the current phase, a colour legend and a hover panel.
why: Likely reason: a plain stage list cannot show how datapoints flow from projects to slides, so the drawing is done on a canvas. The drawing itself lives in the separate fieldEngine file, which keeps this file focused on state and layout.
how: 1. Loads the run record through the data hook, refreshing every few seconds while the run is live. 2. Chooses live, replay or finished mode. 3. Creates the drawing engine on a canvas and feeds it the record. 4. Moves through the stages on a timer or from live progress, and reports the current phase. 5. Renders the top bar, stage list, caption, legend and hover panel. 6. Opens a project's page when a project is clicked.
inputs: tool (Reality Scan or Lessons Learnt), runId, an optional replay flag, an optional onCaughtUp callback and an optional className. The run data comes from the collation API.
outputs: An animated canvas with text overlays. Clicking a project opens its page. The onCaughtUp callback is called when a replay or live animation reaches its end.
risks: Shows only what the run recorded. Replay timing is an approximation and does not match the real length of the run.
debug: If the box stays empty, read the loading and error text inside it, then check the request to the collation endpoint. If the animation freezes, check the mode label and whether the run status is finished. If the canvas is blank, look at the drawing engine. For visual checks in development, the collationAt query setting sets a replay start time.
